subject.title: [Feature]:  Non-blocking heartbeat execution to prevent message processing delays

question: Should OpenClaw add a separate non-blocking heartbeat execution lane or worker model, or continue addressing heartbeat contention through narrower retry, idle, and isolation mitigations?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the requested fix crosses core scheduling, session state, channel delivery, and tool side-effect semantics, so automation cannot safely choose the durable architecture.

options.title: Design Isolated Heartbeat Execution
options.body: Define and implement a maintained heartbeat execution contract with explicit session, delivery, tool, and live-channel proof requirements before code changes.

options.title: Keep Narrow Mitigations
options.body: Continue improving retry cadence, idle gating, isolated sessions, and lightweight context without adding a new execution model.

options.title: Defer For Live Proof
options.body: Wait for a live current-main reproduction with clearer latency requirements before changing heartbeat architecture.

recommendation.title: Design Isolated Heartbeat Execution
recommendation.body: Define and implement a maintained heartbeat execution contract with explicit session, delivery, tool, and live-channel proof requirements before code changes.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest heartbeat runner, wake scheduling, and docs history among the inspected routing candidates.
